questions.q: Define the term "डकसए फेफडलएक्स" (code-mixing) as used in the chapter "जतूह" and give one example from the text where it occurs.
questions.a: Correct answer: Code-mixing refers to the blending of two or more languages within a single utterance, as seen when characters mix Hindi and English in casual conversation (e.g., "ओके, बाई" or "थैंक्यू, सर"). A wrong answer that only gives the linguistic definition without a textual example shows the student cannot ground the term in the specific context of the play.

questions.q: In the dialogue where जतूह says, "ट्यूशन के नाम पर चलने वाला यह फर्जीवाड़ा...", explain why the word "फर्जीवाड़ा" (fraud/racket) is more powerful than "धोखा" (deception) in this context.
questions.a: Correct answer: "फर्जीवाड़ा" implies an organized, systemic, and recurring scam involving multiple stakeholders (schools, tutors, officials), whereas "धोखा" suggests a one-time act by an individual. The former captures the institutionalized corruption theme. A wrong answer treating them as synonyms reveals the student misses the socio-political nuance and the author's critique of the education system.

questions.q: The word "शिक्षा नीति" (education policy) appears in the Director's dialogue: "शिक्षा नीति के अनुसार...". Rewrite this sentence replacing "शिक्षा नीति" with "सरकारी नियम" (government rule) and explain how the shift changes the tone and implication.
questions.a: Correct answer: "सरकारी नियम के अनुसार..." sounds bureaucratic and rigid, removing the aspirational and reformist connotation of "नीति" (policy). The Director uses "नीति" to legitimize his actions; replacing it exposes his hypocrisy. A student who only changes the word without analyzing the tonal shift fails to apply contextual sensitivity.

questions.q: Compare the usage of "ट्यूशन" (tuition) in three different speeches: (a) वफ़र's desperate plea, (b) यथ्यक's sarcastic remark, (c) जतूह's final monologue. How does the same word carry different emotional and thematic weights?
questions.a: Correct answer: For वफ़र, "ट्यूशन" = survival/lifeline (hope); for यथ्यक, "ट्यूशन" = commercial exploitation (cynicism); for जतूह, "ट्यूशन" = systemic disease (indictment). A wrong answer that gives a uniform definition shows inability to analyze how context reshapes meaning across speakers and dramatic moments.

questions.q: Evaluate the author's choice of the word "नैक्यवांक"ख" (accountability) in the climax when जतूह demands it from the Director. Is it the most effective word, or would "ज़िम्मेदारी" (responsibility) or "जवाबदेही" (answerability) work better? Justify.
questions.a: Correct answer: "नैक्यवांक"ख" is the most effective because it carries legal-administrative weight, implying systemic answerability with consequences, unlike "ज़िम्मेदारी" (moral) or "जवाबदेही" (procedural). It matches जतूह's shift from emotional appeal to institutional demand. A student who picks any synonym without justifying the register mismatch fails to evaluate lexical precision in a dramatic climax.

questions.q: Create a new dialogue line for the character ग्स्मेकल्वज (the Director) where he uses the phrase "बैकसडेट" (backdate) to justify an unethical action, mimicking the play's blend of bureaucratic jargon and moral corruption.
questions.a: Criteria for a good answer: The line must (1) use "बैकसडेट" correctly as a verb/noun in a bureaucratic context, (2) reveal the Director's manipulative mindset, (3) maintain the play's tone of casual corruption. Example: "हमने तो बस बैकडेट में दस्तखत करवा लिए, नीति तो वही रहती है।" A poor answer uses the word mechanically without dramatic irony or character voice.
